children: By Xavier Martinez and Lizzy Lawrence

Moderna shares plunged after details from a closely guarded mRNA-based cancer-vaccine study were shared on social media, raising concerns that the treatment might not be as effective as initially hoped.

Moderna's stock fell around 23%, putting the Cambridge, Mass., biotech on pace for its largest decrease since it went public. The results, which appeared largely positive according to analysts, still fell short of the market's heightened expectations.

In August, Moderna's shares more than doubled after announcing the vaccine had prevented melanoma from returning or spreading. The result was hailed as remarkable though experts cautioned it was critical to see the details in the study, which was scheduled to be released on Saturday at the European Society for Medical Oncology conference.
A cancer-focused website OncologyCentral appears to have published some of those results on Thursday, according to screenshots on X.

A key statistic published by the site showed that the vaccine reduced the risk of the cancer spreading by 38% in patients with high-risk melanoma when compared against a standard immunotherapy treatment. TD Cowen analyst Tyler Van Buren said that figure, while favorable, fell short of the market's elevated expectations.

Van Buren added that worsening results between the mid- and late-stage trials could potentially mean that the vaccine would have a lower likelihood of success in cases in which cancer has spread throughout the body or in "more difficult" tumors. Moderna and its partner Merck are studying this vaccine in several types of cancer.
The vaccine also reduced the risk of a recurrence or death from melanoma by 42% in the study, according to the screenshot, a result that Van Buren described as compelling.
Shares of Merck, which is codeveloping the vaccine with Moderna, were flat. Merck and Moderna declined to comment.
Representatives for OncologyCentral and the European Society for Medical Oncology didn't respond to requests for comment.
